2010 U.S. plant-level ethylene nameplate table aggregated to firm. Two source-hierarchy overrides are applied before freezing: Eastman is set to its company-reported 2010 capacity of 458 kt/y (1,010m lb/y), and LyondellBasell to its company-reported U.S. 2010 capacity of 9.6bn lb/y (~4,354 kt/y), which explicitly excludes the permanently shut Chocolate Bayou unit. The resulting internally consistent U.S. denominator is 27,039 kt/y. The contemporaneous 57bn-lb industry figure is retained only as an approximate external reconciliation, not substituted for the auditable firm table.

PVC resin is the frozen exposure basis for the combined PVC/VCM chain because it is the final chain capacity directly comparable across integrated and non-integrated incumbents. Start from the 2010 CMAI North American PVC participant table and contemporaneous 8,118 kt/y NA total; remove Mexican Mexichem (306) and Policyd (235), and remove OxyVinyls Niagara, Canada (590m lb/y ≈268 kt/y) from Oxy’s NA row. Georgia Gulf Sarnia, Canada had permanently closed in 2008. A 26 kt/y source-table residual is retained transparently as Other U.S. residual so shares sum to the reconciled U.S. denominator 7,309 kt/y; it is never assigned to a named incumbent.
